core_obligations: Get finite local freeness of C and choose the factorization f = h o i, so that f' = h' o i' and the Gysin map exists for f' (proof lines 13763-13782).
Use the normal cone presentation and the base change comparison of differentials and conormal sheaves to identify C with the kernel of (g')^* C_{X/P} -> C_{X'/P'} (proof lines 13784-13794).
Apply the excess lemma to get res(i^!) = c_top(C^vee) o (i')^! and conclude using f^! = i^! o h^* and (h')^* = res(h^*) (proof lines 13796-13805).
proof_roadmap: Finiteness of C and the factorization (proof lines 13763-13782).
Identification of C with the conormal kernel (proof lines 13784-13794).
The excess computation and conclusion (proof lines 13796-13805).
difficulty_reason: For a cartesian square of schemes locally of finite type over (S, delta) with both f and f' local complete intersection morphisms and with the Gysin map existing for f, the lemma asserts that C = Ker(H^{-1}((g')^* NL_{X/Y}) -> H^{-1}(NL_{X'/Y'})) is a finite locally free O_{X'}-module, that the Gysin map exists for f', and that res(f^!) = c_top(C^vee) o (f')^! in A^*(X' -> Y') (statement lines 13737-13761). The proof gets finite local freeness of C from More on Algebra, Lemma labelled more-algebra-lemma-base-change-lci-bis, then chooses a factorization f = h o i with h smooth and i an immersion, so that f' = h' o i' with h' and i' the base changes, which also shows the Gysin map exists for f' (proof lines 13763-13782). Using the presentation NL_{X/Y} = (C_{X/P} -> i^* Omega_{P/Y}) of More on Morphisms, Lemma labelled more-morphisms-lemma-get-NL and its primed analogue, together with the identifications (g')^* i^* Omega_{P/Y} = (i')^* Omega_{P'/Y'} by Morphisms, Lemma labelled morphisms-lemma-base-change-differentials and the surjectivity of (g')^* C_{X/P} -> C_{X'/P'} by Morphisms, Lemma labelled morphisms-lemma-conormal-functorial-flat, the proof identifies C with the kernel of that surjection between finite locally free modules (proof lines 13784-13794). Lemma labelled lemma-gysin-excess then gives res(i^!) = c_top(C^vee) o (i')^! in A^*(X' -> P'), and since f^! = i^! o h^*, (f')^! = (i')^! o (h')^* and (h')^* = res(h^*) the conclusion follows (proof lines 13796-13805). Recognising the abstract kernel from the definition of the normal cone as the kernel of the conormal surjection, so that the excess lemma applies, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
